Cross-fitted quantile grids for the debiased mean scan

Source: R/scan_ci.R
crossfit_quantiles.Rd

Splits the rows into folds and predicts, for each fold from models fitted on the other folds, a grid of conditional quantiles of \(Y\) given \(R = 1\) and \(X\), and \(\hat r\), as sharp_scan_mean_ci() requires. The learner is yours. fit_q receives only the observed rows of the training folds and the levels tau = \((k - 1/2)/K\).

Usage

crossfit_quantiles(
  data,
  response,
  fit_q,
  fit_r,
  K = 200L,
  folds = 5L,
  seed = NULL,
  clip = 1e-06
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with all rows, observed and unobserved.

response

Name of the response indicator column (0/1 or logical).

fit_q

function(train, newdata, tau) returning a matrix with one row per row of newdata and one column per level in tau; train holds observed rows.

fit_r

function(train, newdata) returning \(P(R = 1 \mid X)\).

K

Number of quantile levels. Default 200.

folds

Number of folds. Default 5.

seed

Optional seed for the fold assignment.

clip

\(\hat r\) is clipped from below at clip. Default 1e-6.

Value

A list with q (an \(n \times K\) matrix), r and fold, one per row of data.

Details

A smooth location and scale model is a good choice: fit \(\mu(x)\) and \(\sigma(x)\) (for instance with mgcv::gam(..., family = mgcv::gaulss())), and return \(\hat\mu(x) + \hat\sigma(x) \hat F^{-1}(\tau)\), with \(\hat F^{-1}\) the quantiles of the standardised training residuals. quantile_grid() can be used inside fit_q.

See also

sharp_scan_mean_ci(), crossfit_inputs()
